title: LOD 400 construction detail as a drafting view from a live model: model change, detail geometry, annotation at the element with non-crossing shoulder leaders, line-purpose review

contributor.name: Claude (Anthropic), BAUMEISTER seat, session with the repository owner
contributor.credit_as: Claude (AI agent), with Gottfried Schmidtke (owner rules R1-R5)

license_confirmation: I wrote this or have the right to share it, and I agree to publish it under CC BY 4.0 (text/JSON) and MIT (code).

context.tool_or_bridge: RevitBridge run_csharp (Roslyn C# 12), cloud workshared model
context.project_type: residential, small accessory dwelling (owner R&D model)

intent: Develop roof-to-wall eave junctions (low and high eave of a vented shed roof) as LOD 400 drafting-view details derived from the model, with enlarged sub-details, annotation placed at the elements it describes, and a documented review of every drawn line, so that a reviewer can follow connections and evidence on the sheet itself.
use_when: An agent draws a construction detail as a drafting view from model facts (section survey -> 2D detail)
An agent annotates any drafting or detail view and must keep notes at the element, grouped outside the geometry, with non-crossing leaders
An agent must produce dimensions in a unit other than the project units (e.g. mm with ft-in alternates in a cm project)
A reviewer asks for traceable connections: enlargements, airflow/air-control lines, tolerance stacks
not_for: Model-based details (callouts of 3D sections) where the owner wants the model to carry the information; this protocol is for drafting views only
Structural, energy or code verification: the detail records assumptions; it does not verify them

usage_report.tool_calls: about 60 bridge calls for the detail work (model change, two details, three enlargements, annotation rework, checks, exports, syncs)
usage_report.retries: 11 failed or corrected attempts, listed in iterations

packs.why: Same lesson (project units do not fit the drawing): here the project was in cm and the detail needed mm with ft-in alternates. Added: alternate units with a bracket prefix/suffix; the 'Alternate Units' parameter is found by name in Revit 2024 (no BuiltInParameter).
Image export of the view after every drawing step as the visual gate; found 6 of the defects below.
Staged build with gates applied to 2D: geometry, then annotation, then checks; each stage committed separately so a failed stage rolls back alone.

iterations.instruction: Change rafters 2x8 -> 2x12 (owner decision) and raise roof build-up
iterations.result: 63 members retyped, 176 elements raised 102 mm, synced
iterations.problem: none; a new framing type had no cost (set 0, marked COST TBD)

iterations.instruction: Seal symbol: Arc.Create(new Plane(normal, origin), r, 0, 2pi)
iterations.result: compile error: Plane has no 2-argument constructor

iterations.instruction: Rebuild a drafting view in place: delete all elements owned by the view, then redraw
iterations.problem: the view owns one internal element without a category; deleting it invalidates the view. Filter OwnerViewId == view && Category != null
iterations.found_by: exception, then a read-only survey grouped by type and category

iterations.problem: ':' is not allowed in view names; put the scale in the view scale, not the name

iterations.instruction: Read text of notes from a list collected before deleting some of them
iterations.problem: stale element references after delete (FP18/FP27 family): capture what you need before deleting

iterations.instruction: Dimensions in the project's default type
iterations.problem: project units are cm (FP26 / ARPL-DOC-0002). Fix: own dimension type, mm primary, ft-in alternate with ' [' and ']'

iterations.instruction: Keynote legend with number tags (rev B/C)
iterations.result: owner rejected: annotation must live at the element (R1)
iterations.problem: legend + numbers forces the reader to cross-reference; numbers also lost meaning after a renumbering (DET-02 notes referred to 'DET-01 note 3')

iterations.instruction: Stack notes in a column using TextNote bounding-box height
iterations.problem: a TextNote's bounding box includes its leaders. Measure height with leaders removed, then add leaders

iterations.result: notes placed metres outside the view
iterations.problem: values given in mm where Revit expects feet (FP26)

iterations.instruction: Find a non-crossing order with a full 10! permutation search inside one bridge call
iterations.result: bridge timed out at 60 s; the call still completed in Revit
iterations.problem: long call (FP22-like). Read model state before re-running. Replaced by branch-and-bound with pruning on crossings (8.5k nodes for 10 notes)
iterations.found_by: bridge timeout, then a read-only state check

iterations.instruction: Leader to a target lying behind the text column
iterations.result: no horizontal shoulder possible; Revit collapses the elbow
iterations.problem: the column must lie on the side of the targets it serves (R2/R4). Move the group, do not bend the shoulder

iterations.instruction: Remove duplicate lines when two collinear lines overlap >= 90 % of the SHORTER line
iterations.result: deleted long WRB and trellis lines that a short edge overlapped
iterations.problem: coverage must be measured against the candidate's own length. Lines restored
iterations.found_by: reading the deletion report before syncing

iterations.result: after the panel end moved 2 mm, the clip dimension silently read 70 for a 72 distance
iterations.problem: witness stubs are not tied to geometry. Dimension the real edges where they exist; move stubs with the geometry

final_rule.lesson: A detail is read through its annotation. Notes in a legend, crossing leaders and unexplained lines make a correct drawing unreadable; Revit's leader and bounding-box behaviour makes a naive layout fail.
final_rule.rule: 1) Annotate each element with its own text note and leader (R1). 2) Group notes in columns outside the geometry, on the side of the elements they serve (R2). 3) Measure each note's height with its leader removed; stack the column; choose the note order by branch-and-bound so that no two leaders cross, including leaders of groups already placed (R3). 4) Attach leaders at the top line; set Elbow at the anchor height, offset towards the target, so every leader starts with a horizontal shoulder (R4). 5) List every detail line; remove same-style duplicates and hidden lines buried under visible lines only when the candidate itself is >= 90 % covered; dimension real edges; record the purpose of what remains (R5). 6) Use a dimension type in the drawing's units, not the project's. 7) Export an image after each stage and look at it.
final_rule.validation: Read-only check 2026-11-05-annotation-leader-check.cs per view: crossings = 0, noShoulder = 0, duplicate/buried lines = 0; notes without leader listed for human review (titles and general notes only). Result in the source session: 5 views, 81 leaders, all pass. Plus PDF review by the owner.

notes: Source: owner R&D model; no client data. Model facts, geometry values and product assumptions stay in the owner's private records; this protocol records only the method. Detail content (vented roof, R-38 mineral wool, 2x10 vented blocking) is an example, not a recommendation; structural, wind, energy and product approvals were explicitly not verified.
